messages:
incident-bot: P0 alert: Canary group 'inference-api-canary' reporting >30% 5xx and repeated restart/crashloop events across eu-west nodes. Auto-escalation to #incidents. Pager sent to oncall 

alice: ACK I'm on it, switching to oncall context. Investigating canary rollout status and pods.

deploy-bot: Deploy v2.14.1 -> inference-api (canary=10%) started at 2234567899, strategy=rolling update.

alice: checking pods: `kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=inference-api -o wide` shows 3 canary pods, 2 CrashLoopBackOff, 1 Ready but high latency.

carla: seeing real user errors: frontend logs show repeated 502/503 to /v1/generate from eu region, samples: `503 upstream read timeout` and `502 bad gateway` for ~12 minutes. CS pinged.

ben: adding context: HPA recently had change in canary chart — minReplicas set to 0 for canary to save cost. That interacts badly with node drain/rolling update. If pods flake, HPA can scale to 0 and restart/backoff make rollout never recover.

alice: grabbing pod logs for one crashlooping container: `kubectl logs inference-api-7d8f5-c8 --previous -n prod`
```
2026-03-15T10:12:34Z INF Starting server
2026-03-15T10:12:36Z ERR readiness probe failed: http status=502 path=/live check failed
2026-03-15T10:12:36Z INF shutting down
```

carla: readiness probe failures correlate with short terminationGracePeriodSeconds in manifest (set to 0?). Also saw probe timeoutSeconds=1 in canary manifest — too aggressive for cold-starting model server.

dan: I'm on infra. Looking at the deployment manifest that was applied in the canary chart:
```
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /live
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 2
  periodSeconds: 2
  timeoutSeconds: 1
terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 0
```
HPA snippet: `minReplicas: 0` for canary target.

alice: OK that explains flapping: probe timeouts => container restarts => termination=0 => no graceful shutdown => readiness flips while still serving => HPA can scale to 0 in edge windows. Need immediate mitigation: stop the rollout, flip feature flag to disable v2, or roll back. Which is fastest?

ben: fastest is kill the canary traffic or rollback. We have a feature flag for canary routing (router.canary.enabled). Dan, can we flip that remotely?

dan: router service supports flag via config service. I can set `router.canary.enabled=false` and pin traffic to v2 off. Doing it now.

deploy-bot: Config change applied at 2234570100: router.canary.enabled=false. Canary traffic = 0%.

carla: Traffic dropped for canary, frontend errors decreased but some in-flight requests may still error. 5xx rate dropped to baseline within ~90s.

eve: Sent templated message to affected customer contacts: "We're investigating elevated 5xx impacting inference endpoints in EU. Mitigation in progress — we'll follow up with timeline."

alice: While turning canary off stops new canary traffic, the unhealthy canary pods remain on cluster and continue to restart and consume resources. Recommend rollback of deployment and patching manifest to avoid reintroducing the issue.

ben: I propose: 1) rollback canary to previous stable revision, 2) patch canary chart to set readiness timeoutSeconds=10 and terminationGracePeriodSeconds=30, 3) set HPA minReplicas=1 for canary, 4) redeploy canary when tests pass. Any objections?

alice: +1. I'll perform rollback for the canary replica set now: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-api --to-revision=134 -n prod` (this will rollback the deployment image tag for the ReplicaSet).

alice: rollback started at 2234570500. Monitoring pod status...

incident-bot: Pager update: Incident severity remains P1 (service impact). Notifications sent to oncall, SRE, and CS.

ben: While rollback proceeds, patch manifest commands to be ready:
```
kubectl patch deployment inference-api -n prod --type='json' -p='[{
  "op": "replace",
  "path": "/spec/template/spec/terminationGracePeriodSeconds",
  "value": 30
}]'
kubectl patch deployment inference-api -n prod --type='json' -p='[{
  "op": "replace",
  "path": "/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/timeoutSeconds",
  "value": 10
}]'
kubectl patch hpa inference-api-canary -n prod -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":1}}'
```

dan: Applying patches now.

carla: Observability: latency and 5xx graphs show return to normal 3 minutes after rollback finished. Still seeing one older node with evicted pods but not serving traffic.

alice: Rollback completed at 2234570800. Canary pods replaced with stable revision; new pods are healthy.

ben: Patch applied to HPA and deployment template at 2234570900. Confirmed minReplicas=1 and readiness timeout increased.

eve: Customer follow-up: "We rolled back the canary and mitigations are complete. No data loss. We'll share a postmortem with timeline and root cause."

carla: Quick post-incident notes for ticket: root cause = too-aggressive readiness probe + terminationGracePeriodSeconds=0 combined with canary HPA minReplicas=0. This allowed a transient probe flake to escalate into large-scale canary failures and 5xx for EU traffic.

ben: Action items assigned: 
- infra/helm: change canary chart default readiness timeoutSeconds to 10 and terminationGracePeriodSeconds to 30 (owner: dan)
- infra/sre: ensure canary HPA minReplicas >=1 by policy (owner: ben)
- devex: add a canary smoke test that runs readiness checks with initialDelay 5s (owner: carla)
- ops: update runbook to prefer toggling canary flag before rollback when possible (owner: alice)

alice: handing off to next oncall at 2234571200. @ben or @dan please own follow-ups and confirm fixes promoted to staging.

ben: I'll own follow-ups. I'll open the postmortem doc and attach timeline + logs.

incident-bot: Incident closed from P1 -> P0 mitigation at 2234571400 (service recovered, mitigations in place). Please file postmortem within 72 hours.

alice: Thanks team. Final note: no SLA breach expected but we'll quantify exact minutes of customer impact in the postmortem.

carla: +1. Adding reproduction steps to the postmortem: apply manifest with small timeout + minReplicas=0 and run rolling update on a saturated node to reproduce the flapping behavior.

ben: Opening follow-up ticket: INF-4721 with action items and ETA for fixes.

eve: Notifying affected accounts with final update and linking to postmortem when ready.

alice: closing thread, moving to postmortem doc. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
